where: Section 3, the Mr and ωr formula block
problem: The validity note after the formula is corrupted: "where: valid for 0 r is dimensionless; ωr is in rad/s." The condition on ζ has been lost and the sentence cannot be read, so a student cannot tell when Mr and ωr may be used.
fix: "where: valid for 0 ≤ ζ < 1/√2 (about 0.707); r = ω/ωn is dimensionless; ωr is in rad/s; Mr is dimensionless. For ζ ≥ 1/√2 there is no resonant peak."

problem: The example calls the system a unity-feedback system but then applies G(jω) directly to the reference input r(t) = 2 sin(9t). With unity feedback the output follows the closed-loop function T(s) = G/(1+G) = 100/(s² + 6s + 200), so the correct steady-state output is about 1.53 sin(9t − 24.4°), not 3.49 sin(9t − 70.6°). As written, the numbers belong to the open-loop plant.
fix: Drop the words "unity-feedback": "A second-order system has transfer function G(s) = 100/(s² + 6s + 100)." Then the input is applied at the plant input and G(jω) gives the output. If the closed-loop answer is wanted, keep unity feedback and use T(j9) = 100/(119 + j54), giving gain 0.765 and phase −24.4°.

problem: "|G(jω)| is dimensionless gain" is true only when input and output have the same units. A motor with voltage input and speed output has a gain in rad/s per volt, and the statement will mislead.
fix: "|G(jω)| is the gain, output amplitude divided by input amplitude (dimensionless when input and output share the same units)."

problem: M at ω = 9 rad/s comes out as 1.747, the same number as Mr, only because 9 rad/s is close to ωr = 9.06 rad/s. A student may conclude that M equals Mr at any test frequency.
fix: Add one line: "M at the test frequency happens to be close to Mr because 9 rad/s is near ωr = 9.06 rad/s; at any other frequency M would be smaller."
